svg.title: Can the past predict next quarter's spending?
svg.desc: Left: quarterly growth of US real spending per person on non-durable goods and services, 1953 to 2026, and the regression's prediction from spending and income growth two to four quarters back, fitted on 1953 to 2019 (in-sample R squared 11.5 per cent). Right: R squared by sample, with lags two to four (the headline) and with lags one to four, where averaging within quarters adds predictability even under Hall's hypothesis; diamonds: lags two to four on total spending, durables included. Hall's 1978 benchmark for forward-looking households is zero. Educational demos made to show an open-source tool. Not research.
